items.title: Survivors uncover new evidence in Australia’s contaminated blood scandal
items.description: The 1980s contaminated blood crisis devastated the lives of thousands of Australians who were infected with hepatitis C or HIV. Now, survivor Tristan Stanley, who contracted hep C as a child, has uncovered government documents that raise troubling questions about the scandal.

items.title: Britain's new PM is redefining populist anger
items.description: Britain's new left-leaning PM Andy Burnham has seized the same public discontent driving Nigel Farage on the populist right but with a very different agenda. As One Nation climbs in the polls, Australia should be paying attention.

items.title: After a big defeat, US pro-Israel lobby sets sights on midterms
items.description: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee lobby group boasts of its track record of success deciding election-winners as it endorses candidates that support its cause.

items.title: Iron deficiency from too much cow's milk a 'hidden health crisis' for toddlers
items.description: Paediatricians across Australia are concerned about a jump in iron deficiency in young children due to excess cow's milk, and the need to better educate parents about the issue.

items.title: Bird flu is spreading across Australia — this is what you need to know
items.description: There are more than a hundred confirmed cases of the deadly H5N1 bird flu strain across Australia. Here's how it spreads and what to know.

items.title: Maps show Ukraine's extensive reach into Russian territory
items.description: Ukraine's 40-day campaign to take the war to the heart of Russia has increased the strain on Russian businesses, people and air defences, analysts say.

items.title: Here are the questions asked in Australia's first complete census
items.description: When you sit down to fill in the census, you will be taking part in an ancient human tradition.

items.title: These young women are redefining who belongs in agriculture
items.description: A university program challenges the idea that women need to grow up on a farm to build a career in agriculture.

items.title: Sandwich generation navigating work, elderly parents and kids at home
items.description: Broadcaster and author Sarah Macdonald is part of a growing army of silent unpaid workers, coping with the consequences of a housing crisis and a broken aged care system.

items.title: Ukraine denies targeting Bulgaria after drone explodes near pipeline
items.description: Ukraine has denied targeting Bulgaria after a drone entered Bulgaria's airspace exploded close to the strategic Trans-Balkan gas pipeline near the Romanian border.

items.title: Iran says Hormuz deal 'close' but reopening depends on other conditions
items.description: Iran and Oman are "very close" to reaching an accord on a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's foreign minister says. This is your three-minute briefing on the key developments overnight in the Middle East.

items.title: Six times our politicians reminded us not to take politics too seriously
items.description: Over the past 25 years of Insiders covering Australian politics, the art of it has sometimes been more finger painting than masterpiece.

items.title: 'Very debilitating': Hunter Biden opens up about his father's cancer
items.description: Former US president Joe Biden's prostate cancer has spread to other parts of his body and is causing him pain, even as he continues to speak out on public issues, according to his son Hunter.

items.title: 'I felt I wasn't worthy': Para athletes on barriers in elite sport
items.description: Paralympic gold medallist Nikki Ayers walked away from rowing, feeling devalued in the sport. She's not alone; disabled athletes have told ABC Sport they face discrimination and burnout due to a lack of funding and support.

items.title: The race is on in a secret location to save one of our rarest orchids
items.description: It takes years of work, dozens of volunteers, picky pollinators and a special fungus to save Australia’s endangered orchids. Here's why people drive from all over the country to do it anyway.

items.title: 'If we don't tour, we don't eat': The Drones return after 10 years
items.description: It's been a decade between The Drones's shows and albums, but demand for their reunion proves this "feral little band" still matters deeply.

items.title: Do you believe in life after love? What about music quizzes?
items.description: Can you feel something inside you say 'Try your hand at the Spicks and Specks quiz'? Well, you've come to the right place.

items.title: Seal numbers on Victorian island plummet as pollution affects pups
items.description: Deen Maar Island was once home to Australia's largest fur seal colony before the pups started developing alopecia.

items.title: Gina Rinehart says ABC Ombudsman finding 'fails all Australian women'
items.description: The mining magnate says the ABC's Editorial Standards need "significant improvement" after a video describing a fictional scenario that involved a violent attack on her was aired on Race Around the World.

items.title: Perth man allegedly damaged 20 cars during 90-minute rampage
items.description: Police charge a 45-year-old who allegedly got out of his car and smashed several stationary vehicles, before leading officers on a wild chase through Perth's northern suburbs.

items.title: China braces for Typhoon Dolphin after storm lashes Japan's southern islands
items.description: Typhoon Dolphin has lashed Japan's southern islands of Okinawa and turned towards China, where it is expected to make landfall late Sunday or early Monday local time.

items.title: Trump announces $560m critical minerals investment in tiny NSW town
items.description: The Pentagon is investing more than half a billion dollars to expand an Australian critical mineral project poised to become the world's first scandium mine.

items.title: Todd Blanche confirmed as US attorney general after divisive hearing
items.description: The vote follows a tumultuous confirmation fight that exposed concerns — from some Republicans as well as Democrats — about putting Donald Trump's former defence lawyer in charge of a Justice Department that historically prides itself on its independence from the White House.

items.title: Oats, water, salt the winning ingredients for porridge-making champ
items.description: A former cafe owner from Sydney has been crowned Australia's porridge-making champion at an inaugural competition on the New South Wales Central Coast.

items.title: Flowers blooming, birds swooping amid unusually warm 'sprinter'
items.description: An early magpie swooping season, underwhelming ski season and canola crops blooming a month in advance are some signs of an unusually warm winter across NSW.
